claims.text: Google says the actor used compromised cloud infrastructure and an AI coding system to plan, build and execute credential harvesting in less than six hours.
claims.sourceLocator: Executive summary and Bespoke Vulnerability Scanning and Credential Harvesting Campaign

claims.text: Google says the framework managed scanning, troubleshooting, credential harvesting and IP rotation and compromised thousands of third-party credentials.

claims.text: Google separately describes a dashboard managing more than 23,800 harvested secrets.

claims.text: The report does not establish that the under-six-hour campaign and the dashboard are the same incident.
claims.sourceLocator: Separately labelled examples; article keeps them separate

claims.text: Google says a PRC-linked agentic framework effort stayed at the build stage and associated assets were disabled.
GTIG says it has not observed fully autonomous pipelines deployed against targets in the wild.
Sysdig observed an exposed Ollama server powering a staged offensive tool aimed only at private practice ranges while still under development, with ultimate intent uncertain.
claims.sourceLocator: Opening, development, targets and intent sections

claims.text: Google says DUSTMAKER modified hidden .claude, .vscode and .cursor paths and could establish build or startup execution.
Google assesses that adversarial JavaScript comments were intended to trigger refusals or skipped analysis by LLM security scanners.
Google says the DUSTMAKER activity triggered Gemini safety responses.
NIST CAISI reports more than 250,000 attempts from over 400 participants across 13 models, with at least one successful hijack against every target and no uniform correlation with general capability.
Google says an exposed GitHub PAT enabled an April intrusion involving unauthorized AI infrastructure, privilege changes, credential discovery and quota requests.
claims.sourceLocator: Illicit Account Procurement and Infrastructure Compromise; Table 11

claims.text: NIST's draft concept proposes distinct agent identities, managed authorization and delegation, action visibility and data provenance.
The practical security boundary is the model plus instructions, tools, identities, data paths and infrastructure.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us synthesis from incident paths and control context

claims.text: Agents should have bounded identities, tools and privileged operations.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us recommendation from Table 11 and NIST control areas

claims.text: Workspaces, instruction files, hooks and tool descriptions should be treated as untrusted inputs.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us recommendation from DUSTMAKER and hijacking evidence

notes: Recast repeated contrast formulas into direct evidence-and-consequence reasoning, especially in the opening and control recommendations.
Tightened the autonomy boundary and kept Google's under-six-hour campaign separate from its separately described 23,800-secret dashboard.
Reduced thesis repetition in the close while preserving the six practical controls, every attribution and caveat, and Australian English.
Reviewed the final inline SVG against ArticleArtwork.astro and rendered existing artwork; it is original, responsive, accessible, script-free and clearly labelled as conceptual rather than evidence.
